IFRS16_Sample.q: Under IFRS 16, which of the following leases is NOT exempt from recognition on the balance sheet?
opt: A 10-month lease for office space with no renewal option
A 6-month lease for a company car
A lease for a laptop with a fair value of $4,500
IFRS16_Sample.ex: Option 4. Long-term leases (12+ months) must be recognized. Exemptions: (1) short-term leases ≤12 months, (2) low-value assets < $5,000 (laptops, office furniture). A 15-year lease clearly exceeds the short-term threshold.

IFRS16_Sample.q: What is the correct treatment of initial direct costs incurred by a lessee under IFRS 16?
opt: Expense them immediately in profit or loss
Include them in the measurement of the Right-of-Use Asset
Deduct them from the Lease Liability
Recognize them as a prepayment and amortize over the lease term
IFRS16_Sample.ex: Option 2. Initial direct costs (e.g., legal fees, commissions) are INCLUDED in the ROU Asset measurement, not expensed. This is different from the previous IAS 17 treatment. Remember: ROU Asset = Lease Liability + Initial Direct Costs + Prepayments - Incentives.

IFRS16_Sample.q: A company enters into a 5-year lease with annual payments of $50,000 payable at the end of each year. The implicit interest rate is 8%. Calculate the initial Lease Liability (rounded to nearest $). Present Value annuity factor for 5 years at 8% = 3.993.
IFRS16_Sample.ex: Lease Liability = $50,000 × 3.993 = $199,650. The initial lease liability is measured at the present value of lease payments. Using the annuity factor: $50,000 × 3.993 = $199,650. This forms the basis for both the ROU Asset and subsequent interest calculations.

IFRS16_Sample.q: A lessee has a Lease Liability of $200,000 at the start of Year 1. Annual lease payment is $50,000, and the interest rate is 8%. Calculate the Interest Expense for Year 1.
IFRS16_Sample.ex: Interest Expense = $200,000 × 8% = $16,000. Interest is calculated on the opening lease liability balance using the effective interest method. This $16,000 interest + $34,000 principal repayment = $50,000 total payment. Year 2 liability will be $200,000 - $34,000 = $166,000.

IAS36_Sample.q: Which of the following assets does NOT require mandatory annual impairment testing under IAS 36?
opt: Goodwill acquired in a business combination
An intangible asset with an indefinite useful life
Property, plant, and equipment with a 20-year useful life
An intangible asset not yet available for use
IAS36_Sample.ex: Option 3. PPE with finite useful life does NOT require annual testing — only when impairment indicators exist. Mandatory annual testing applies to: (1) Goodwill, (2) Intangibles with indefinite lives, (3) Intangibles not yet available for use.

IAS36_Sample.q: Under IAS 36, how is the recoverable amount of an asset determined?
opt: The lower of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use
The higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use
The carrying amount of the asset
The net realizable value of the asset
IAS36_Sample.ex: Option 2 — the HIGHER of the two. Recoverable Amount = Higher of (Fair Value Less Costs of Disposal, Value in Use). This ensures assets are written down only when BOTH measures fall below carrying amount. Remember: We want to maximize the recoverable amount.

IAS36_Sample.q: An asset has a carrying amount of $500,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is $420,000. Its value in use is $460,000. What is the impairment loss?
IAS36_Sample.ex: Impairment Loss = $500,000 - $460,000 = $40,000. Recoverable Amount = Higher of ($420,000, $460,000) = $460,000. Since carrying amount ($500,000) > recoverable amount ($460,000), recognize $40,000 impairment loss.

IAS36_Sample.q: A Cash-Generating Unit has: Goodwill $100,000, Equipment $300,000, Building $500,000. Total carrying amount = $900,000. Recoverable amount = $700,000. After impairment, what is the carrying amount of the Equipment?
IAS36_Sample.ex: Equipment = $250,000. Step 1: Allocate $100,000 impairment to goodwill first (reduces to $0). Step 2: Remaining impairment = $900,000 - $700,000 - $100,000 = $100,000. Step 3: Allocate pro-rata to Equipment and Building: Equipment = $300,000 × ($100,000 / $800,000) = $37,500 reduction. New Equipment = $300,000 - $50,000 = $250,000. (Note: Simplified calculation shown; exact pro-rata allocation.)
